# AgentShield: Complete Technical Reference & AI Architecture Guide

> Open-Source Zero-Leak Secret Defense & Sandboxing for Autonomous AI Coding Agents
> Canonical URL: https://agentshield.ritualdev.in/

> Repository: https://github.com/RitualDev-Lab/AgentShield
> Author: RitualDev Lab (https://github.com/RitualDev-Lab)
> License: Apache-2.0

## 1. System Overview & Problem Statement
Autonomous AI coding agents (such as Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, OpenAI Codex, and Google Antigravity) execute shell commands, read local files, and communicate with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers using developer privileges. When inspecting codebases to resolve issues, agents frequently execute operations like `cat .env`, run shell scripts containing exported API keys, or include active credentials in Git commits.

AgentShield solves this security vulnerability by providing a zero-leak, deterministic defense layer running locally on the developer workstation and in CI/CD pipelines.

## 2. Key Architecture Pillars
- **Zero-Telemetry, Local-First Runtime**: All inspections, pattern evaluations, entropy calculations, and redactions occur entirely in-memory on the host machine. No code, tokens, or telemetry leave the system.
- **Active Shannon Entropy Discovery**: Computes Shannon entropy H = -sum(p * log2(p)) over candidate alphanumeric tokens [a-zA-Z0-9+/=_-]{20,128}. Candidate strings exceeding H >= 4.5 bits/char without repetitive character structures are identified as unknown high-entropy secrets.
- **Collision-Resistant Surrogate Tokens**: Replaces identified credentials with deterministic 16-hex SHA-256 tokens (`[AGENT_SHIELD:ID:hexHash]`), guaranteeing mathematical 1:1 bijection and zero token collision upon local rehydration.
- **AST Shell Command Sandboxing**: Tokenizes and normalizes compound commands, unpacking subshell wrappers (`sh -c "..."`, `bash -c '...'`) and bash ANSI-C escapes (`$'cat\\t.env'`) to intercept unauthorized file reading (`grep`, `awk`, `dd`, `python -c ...`, input redirection `< .env`).
- **MCP Protocol Interceptor**: Evaluates bidirectional JSON-RPC requests across Model Context Protocol server tools, scrubbing arguments and inbound responses.
- **Tamper-Evident HMAC Audit Ledger**: Chained cryptographic event entries with sequence numbers and previous-hash verification preventing log manipulation.

## 3. Command Line Interface (CLI)
- `npx @ritualdev_lab/agentshield scan <file>`: Scans a file and outputs findings with redacted previews (supports `--json` and `--include-raw`).
- `npx @ritualdev_lab/agentshield redact <file>`: Emits sanitized text with credentials replaced by surrogate tokens.
- `npx @ritualdev_lab/agentshield stream`: Real-time stdin-to-stdout stream redactor for terminal pipes.
- `npx @ritualdev_lab/agentshield exec "<command>"`: Sandboxes agent execution and redacts stdout/stderr in flight.
- `npx @ritualdev_lab/agentshield hook git-install`: Installs non-destructive Git pre-commit hook in `.git/hooks/pre-commit`.
- `npx @ritualdev_lab/agentshield hook check`: Audits staged Git diffs and rejects sensitive file commits.
- `npx @ritualdev_lab/agentshield ci --base <ref>`: Audits pull request diffs in CI/CD workflows and generates Markdown/SARIF reports.
- `npx @ritualdev_lab/agentshield compliance <file>`: Audits findings against SOC2, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, and ISO27001 regulatory controls.

## 4. Frequently Asked Questions (AEO/GEO Index)

### How does AgentShield differ from traditional secret scanners like Gitleaks or Trufflehog?
Traditional tools are post-hoc scanners designed to alert after secrets are already written to disk or committed to Git. AgentShield acts as an active runtime sandbox that intercepts agent tool calls and commands in real time, redacting tokens from entering LLM context windows and replacing them with local surrogate placeholders.

### Can AgentShield work offline without internet access?
Yes. AgentShield is 100% self-contained and operates in air-gapped environments with zero external network calls or cloud dependencies.

### What AI coding assistants are supported?
AgentShield supports all terminal-based and MCP-compatible coding agents, including Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex, Antigravity, and custom agent loops.

## 5. Threat Model Alignment: OWASP LLM02 and MITRE ATLAS

Security reviewers map AgentShield onto the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and the MITRE ATLAS knowledge base. This section is the canonical mapping; `docs/llms.txt` carries the short form.

| Framework reference | Risk | AgentShield control | CLI surface |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OWASP LLM02:2025 | Sensitive Information Disclosure | Deterministic surrogate substitution (`[AGENT_SHIELD:ID:hexHash]`) before any tool result reaches the agent | `scan`, `redact`, `stream`, `exec` |
| OWASP LLM01:2025 | Prompt Injection | Shell-boundary enforcement: injected instructions cannot produce a plaintext secret even when the model complies | `exec` |
| OWASP LLM05:2025 | Improper Output Handling | In-flight redaction of subprocess stdout/stderr, including interpreter output | `exec`, `stream` |
| OWASP LLM06:2025 | Excessive Agency | High-risk read paths intercepted and reported instead of executed | `exec`, `hook check`, `ci` |
| MITRE ATLAS AML.T0025 | Exfiltration via Cyber Means | AST normalization unpacks subshells, ANSI-C quoting, and redirection before evaluation | `exec` |
| MITRE ATLAS AML.T0057 | LLM Data Leakage | Surrogate substitution on the data path between repository and context window | `scan`, `redact`, `stream` |
| MITRE ATLAS AML.T0086 | Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation | Bidirectional MCP JSON-RPC argument and response scrubbing | `exec` (MCP proxy) |
| MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051 | LLM Prompt Injection | Cross-turn taint graph flags multi-turn secret laundering | `exec`, ledger |

Every finding emitted by `agentshield scan --json` carries the entropy score, the matched pattern family, and the redacted preview needed to attribute the finding to the controls above.

## 6. Runnable Deployment Examples

The three examples below are the deployment paths reviewers ask about most often: containerized use, commit-time gating, and verification that wrapper tricks do not defeat the sandbox.

### 6.1 Docker containerization defense

Pin the published CLI in a thin image so the same scanner binary is used locally and in CI:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile.agentshield
FROM node:22-alpine
RUN npm install --global @ritualdev_lab/agentshield@0.1.3
WORKDIR /workspace
ENTRYPOINT ["agentshield"]
```

```bash
# Build once
docker build -f Dockerfile.agentshield -t agentshield:local .

# Gate a build on the presence of secrets in the working tree
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workspace -w /workspace agentshield:local scan .env --json

# Run an agent command inside the sandbox; stdout is redacted in flight
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workspace -w /workspace agentshield:local exec "cat .env"

# Audit a pull-request diff and emit a Markdown report
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workspace -w /workspace agentshield:local \
  ci --base origin/main --report .agentshield-report.md
```

`docker run` with a read-only mount is sufficient for auditing because AgentShield never needs write access outside `.git`:

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workspace:ro -w /workspace agentshield:local scan .env
```

### 6.2 Pre-commit Git hook configuration

AgentShield ships two hook definitions in `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` (`agentshield` for the secret gate and `agentshield-audit` for agent-permission auditing). Add them to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/RitualDev-Lab/AgentShield
    rev: v0.1.3
    hooks:
      - id: agentshield
      - id: agentshield-audit
```

```bash
# Install the framework and activate the hooks
pre-commit install
pre-commit run --all-files
```

When the project does not use the `pre-commit` framework, the bundled installer writes a non-destructive hook directly:

```bash
npx @ritualdev_lab/agentshield hook git-install
npx @ritualdev_lab/agentshield hook check
```

The same gate belongs in CI so a hook bypass cannot reach `main`:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/agentshield.yml
name: AgentShield
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  secret-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: RitualDev-Lab/AgentShield@main
        with:
          base_ref: origin/${{ github.base_ref }}
          fail_on_leak: "true"
```

### 6.3 AST shell bypass neutralization

The sandbox tokenizes and normalizes a command before deciding, so a wrapper that a naive string match would miss is reduced to the command it actually runs.

| Bypass form | Normalized form | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cat .env` | `cat .env` | blocked |
| `sh -c "cat .env"` | subshell unwrapped to `cat .env` | blocked |
| `bash -c 'grep . .env'` | subshell unwrapped to `grep . .env` | blocked |
| `$'cat\t.env'` | ANSI-C escape decoded to `cat .env` | blocked |
| `cat < .env` | input redirection from a secret file | blocked |
| `python -c "open('.env').read()"` | interpreter one-liner reading a secret file | blocked |
| `env \| sort` | environment dump | redacted |
| `curl -H "Authorization: $API_KEY" https://example.com` | variable expansion of a known secret | redacted |

Reproduce each row locally:

```bash
agentshield exec "cat .env"
agentshield exec "sh -c 'cat .env'"
agentshield exec "bash -c 'grep . .env'"
agentshield exec '$'"'"'cat\t.env'"'"'
agentshield exec "cat < .env"
agentshield exec "python -c \"open('.env').read()\""
agentshield exec "env | sort"
```

Streams that never pass through `exec` are still covered:

```bash
cat .env | agentshield stream
agentshield scan .env --json | head -n 20
```

## 7. Verification and Test Evidence

The checks below are the ones referenced in the pull request that introduced this section; they require no network access beyond the identifier lookups and no build step.

```bash
# 1. Every fenced code block is balanced (expect an even count per file)
grep -c '^```' docs/llms.txt docs/llms-full.txt

# 2. No unbalanced inline backticks
grep -o '`' docs/llms.txt | wc -l

# 3. The framework indexes cited above resolve
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -L https://atlas.mitre.org/
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -L https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -L https://owasp.org/www-project-top-10-for-large-language-model-applications/

# 4. The documents contain no credential-shaped material
grep -nE '(sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY)' \
  docs/llms.txt docs/llms-full.txt

# 5. Optional: run the project's own scanner over the new text
npx @ritualdev_lab/agentshield scan docs/llms.txt
npx @ritualdev_lab/agentshield scan docs/llms-full.txt
```

The repository keeps near-identical copies of both manifests at the project root (`llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`). They are intentionally left untouched here so the maintainer's own publication step (`scripts/sync-wiki.cjs`) remains the single source of truth for that duplication.
